thesis.counterparty: Retail/algo liquidity takers and passive alt market makers who are still quoting off the pre-shock price during the lag window; they are the ones who transact (or get run over) at the stale price before the alt catches up to BTC's already-realized move. The bot's maker entry effectively front-runs their repricing.
thesis.evidence: (1) Business Perspectives' tick-by-tick BTC-vs-Cardano lead-lag study reports a measured BTC-leads-ADA lead time of 16-118 seconds, mean ~57 seconds -- direct evidence BTC is the price leader and ADA reprices with a lag, though at a much shorter timescale than this 1h-bar thesis uses (a scale-mismatch caveat, not a refutation: the mechanism -- differential reaction speed -- is the same one this thesis stretches to an hourly trigger with a several-hour resolution window). (2) DergiPark/PressAcademia 'Bitcoin's Lagged Effect on Altcoins: A Short-Term Research' (VAR model) finds daily short-term-lagged BTC values have a positive, significant relationship with ETH, ADA and BNB, but explicitly NOT with XRP -- motivating this thesis's universe choice (ETH/ADA/XRP/SOL tested; XRP's weaker literature support is a known risk flagged here, not hidden). (3) Countervailing evidence noted for honesty: Aslanidis et al. (Finance Research Letters, 2021, NARDL model on ETH/XRP/LTC 2015-2019) find BTC's negative shocks have a LARGER effect on altcoins than positive shocks of equal size -- i.e. their asymmetry runs opposite in sign/direction detail to what this thesis's exploratory probe found (see exploratory/cross_asset/probe_btc_lag.out.txt: down-shocks showed a bounce, not amplified continuation, in the 2025-2026 long_1h sample) -- which is exactly why this thesis registers ONLY the up-shock/long side and treats the down side as unresolved rather than symmetric.
thesis.mechanism: BTC is the most liquid, most-arbed instrument in the market and absorbs new information first; thinner-book alt market makers (ETH/ADA/XRP/SOL here) observe and reprice a BTC shock with a measurable lag because their own order flow and cross-venue arb links are slower/thinner. During that lag window the alt's quoted price is stale relative to the new BTC-implied fair value.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 5 is a cross-sectional rank/long-short book across ~100-470 names that collapses when trimmed to a handful of positions. This thesis trades each of 4 alts independently off one shared exogenous trigger (BTC's own realized shock) -- no basket, no ranking, no short leg, no dilution mechanism to fail.

Row 13 (BTC-TSM) is BTC trading its OWN price trend against its own history. Here BTC is never traded at all -- it is only read as an exogenous trigger so a DIFFERENT, slower-reacting asset can be traded. The mechanism is inter-asset information diffusion lag, not own-asset time-series momentum.

Row 12 is a 12-coin basket average diluted by uncorrelated names. This thesis has no basket average -- each symbol's trades are simulated and reported independently in screen.run_screen, so one weak name cannot dilute another's edge.

Row 76 is multi-day mean-reversion over an overnight window (price reverting to a prior level). This is a continuation/momentum mechanism over a 6-hour lag following a shock, not mean reversion, and does not use an overnight session boundary.

thesis.prediction: Following an hour in which BTC's own return exceeds +60 bps, each of ETH/ADA/XRP/SOL will show a positive mean forward return over the next 6 hours that is materially larger than its unconditional mean forward return over the same dataset — i.e. the alt keeps drifting up after the BTC shock instead of the move being fully priced in within the same hour. If a bootstrap CI95 on screened net bps (after the 11.5 bps cost) does not exclude zero, or WR < p*(150 bps)=53.83%, the thesis is falsified.
thesis.signal_py:
import pandas as pd
from research.swarm.lib import load_data as ld


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Long-only: fires 1 when BTC's own PRIOR closed 1h bar returned > 60 bps, on the
    theory that this alt (ETH/ADA/XRP/SOL) reprices the shock with a multi-hour lag.
    Uses only BTC bars with ts <= the current alt bar's ts (merge_asof backward) so no
    future information ever enters the signal at any truncation point.
    """
    btc = ld.load_ohlcv("BTC", "1h", era="train", dataset="long_1h")
    btc_ret_prior = btc["close"].pct_change().shift(1)

    b = btc_ret_prior.rename("btc_ret_prior").reset_index()
    b.columns = ["ts", "btc_ret_prior"]
    b = b.sort_values("ts")

    alt_ts = pd.DataFrame({"ts": df.index}).sort_values("ts")
    merged = pd.merge_asof(alt_ts, b, on="ts", direction="backward")
    merged = merged.set_index("ts").reindex(df.index)

    thresh = 0.006
    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[merged["btc_ret_prior"] > thresh] = 1
    return sig

spec.doa_line: Kill if, on the frozen long_1h train screen, n<30 OR bootstrap CI95 of net bps includes 0 OR observed WR < p*(150bps)=53.83% (fee_math.p_star), OR the ±20% tp_bps robustness read (STANDARDS #9: 120bps and 180bps variants) flips net_bps_mean sign in either variant.
